scope: Firefox and WebKit/Safari launch availability only; no app navigation, account creation, workflow changes, or lifecycle test performed
acceptanceStatus: blocked; Firefox and WebKit privacy acceptance criteria remain unverified

localRunnerPreflight.interpretation: No ready local alternative found. This does not establish that browsers cannot be provisioned in another environment.

bridge.inspection: Created and closed an empty default context; context.browser() returned a browser whose browserType().name() was "chromium". The exposed BrowserType is Chromium only; no Firefox or WebKit BrowserType was available through the documented bridge.
bridge.limitation: The documented bridge has no Firefox/WebKit BrowserType to call launch() on. No alternate BrowserType/import/property was guessed or used. Therefore these are supported-API limitations, not browser launch errors.

firefox.limitation: No executable found at the checked locations, and the bridge does not expose a Firefox BrowserType.

webkitSafari.limitation: No executable found at the checked locations, and the bridge does not expose a WebKit BrowserType. Native Safari is not available in this environment.

conclusion.applicationResult: not tested; no application pass or failure inferred

acceptanceEvidence.reason: Neither requested engine could be launched; no simulated lifecycle events or Chromium substitutes were used.

resumeRequirements.environment: A browser runner exposing actual Firefox and WebKit BrowserTypes and their compatible installed executables, with access to the app and its test-account cleanup adapter.
resumeRequirements.test: Serve a production frontend bundle, create fresh scoped accounts/cases, and run the summary/detail A-to-B native-history journey in each engine. Require trusted pageshow.persisted=true, concealment at pageshow and first animation frame, concealment throughout fresh /api/me, then only the matching identity; verify scoped cleanup.
resumeRequirements.classification: Keep unavailable engine, ordinary reload without BFCache, and demonstrated application failure as separate outcomes. WebKit testing is not proof of native Safari testing.
